chunks: Al-Tawhid: My father, from Sa'd, from Ibn Isa, from Ibn Fadhal, from al-Halabi and Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is One, Compact, He does not have any hollowness, while the spirit (al-Ruh) is a creation from among His creations and is an aid, support and power which Allah places in the hearts of the messengers and believers.
ai.seo_question: What is the nature of the Ruh (Spirit) in Shia theology according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Shaykh al-Mufid’s chain in *Al-Tawhid* clarifies the attribute of *Al-Samad* by negating physical hollowness (*juf*), aligning with the Shia doctrine of divine incorporeality. It further elucidates the nature of *Al-Ruh* not as a separate divine essence, but as a created force of victory and strength instilled by God into the hearts of prophets and believers, distinguishing it from the soul or breath.

en.ammaar-muslim: 4. [4/301] al-Tawhid: My father from Sa’d from Ibn Isa from Ibn Fadhal from al-Halabi and Zurara from Abi Abdillahعليه السلام  who said:

Allah Blessed and Elevated is One, Compact, He does not have any hollowness, while the spirit (al-Ruh) is a creation from among His creations and is an aid, support and power which Allah places in the hearts of the messengers and believers.
